heading: accept()
content: Accepts a pending connection on a socket. Returns a new socket object usable to send and receive data on the connection, and the address bound to the socket on the other end.

heading: bind(address)
content: Bind the socket to address. The socket must not already be bound. The format of address depends on the address family — see socket module documentation for details on af_inet, af_inet6, and af_unix.

heading: close()
content: Mark the socket closed. The underlying system resource is freed. All future operations on the socket object will fail. See also shutdown() for partial connection closing.

heading: connect(address)
content: Connect to a remote socket at address. The format of address depends on the address family. If the connection is interrupted by a signal, the method waits until the connection completes. Raises socket.timeout on timeout.

heading: getpeername()
content: Return the remote address to which the socket is connected. This is useful to find the port number of a remote IPv4/v6 socket. The format of the returned address depends on the address family.

heading: getsockname()
content: Return the socket's own address. This is useful to find the port number of an IPv4/v6 socket.

heading: listen(backlog)
content: Enable a server to accept connections. backlog specifies the number of unaccepted connections the system will allow before refusing new connections. If not specified, a default reasonable value is chosen.

heading: recv(bufsize)
content: Receive data from the socket. The return value is a bytes object representing the data received. The maximum amount of data to be received at once is specified by bufsize.

heading: send(data)
content: Send data to the socket. The socket must be connected to a remote socket. Returns the number of bytes sent. Applications are responsible for checking that all data has been sent.

heading: setsockopt(level, optname, value)
content: Set the value of the given socket option. The needed symbolic constants are defined in the socket module (SO_* etc). The value argument can either be an integer or a bytes object.

heading: shutdown(how)
content: Shut down one or both halves of the connection. If how is SHUT_RD, further receives are disallowed. If SHUT_WR, further sends. If SHUT_RDWR, both.
